body:
## Twenty Questions for a Prediction

A doctor asks one yes-or-no question, then chooses the next question from the answer. After a short path, the patient reaches a recommendation.

A decision tree predicts the same way. Each split asks whether one feature falls on one side of a boundary.

The final leaf stores an answer or a mix of answers from training examples that reached it.
common_mistakes: Growing until every training row has its own leaf.
Reading one greedy split as the only valid explanation.
Ignoring the advantage given to features with many possible cut points.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Twenty Questions for a Prediction” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Trees handle curved rules and mixed features while remaining inspectable.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Twenty Questions for a Prediction” story, explain Decision Trees without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
